title: gpu oom and cuda/library mismatch debugging notes - riley carter
content:
Context:
- Notebook / local dev machine (dev-01, Ubuntu 22.04) and a nightly CI runner (ci-gpu-2) started hitting intermittent CUDA OOMs when running the same model (gpt-ish medium, batch_size 8).
- Issue first seen after upgrading container base image + PyTorch wheel on 2024-02-14.
- Symptoms: immediate OOM on first forward for some models; in other cases, driver/runtime mismatch errors appear in logs.

Commands run (host and inside container):
- Host checks:
  - nvidia-smi
    -> Driver Version: 525.85.12, CUDA Version (reported): 12.0
    -> 8 GPUs, some processes listed (kworker, previous runs).
  - sudo modinfo nvidia | grep -i version
    -> shows 525.85.12

- Container checks:
  - docker run --gpus all --rm -it --entrypoint bash my-image:latest
  - python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.cuda.device_count()); sys.exit(0)"
    -> torch 2.1.0+cu118, cuda runtime version=11.8, torch.cuda.is_available() = True, device_count = 1 (weird: host has 8)
  - python -c "from ctypes import CDLL; CDLL('libcudart.so')"
    -> inside container, some libcudart resolves, but ldd on libtorch_cuda.so shows missing symbols (see below).
  - ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep not
    -> several compat entries; "libcuda.so.1 => not found" occasionally for older images (container variant).

- Repro steps that trigger OOM quickly:
  - python -m scripts/serve_model --model gpt-medium --batch_size 8 --seq_len 2048
  - logs: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.0 GiB (GPU 0; 8.00 GiB total capacity; 6.11 GiB already allocated; 512.00 MiB free; 7.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  - other runs: RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error

Error snippets seen in different runs: (copied verbatim)
- "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime"
- "libcudnn.so.8: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.05 GiB (GPU 0; 14.76 GiB total capacity; 13.83 GiB already allocated; 933.94 MiB free; 13.92 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- "cudaErrorIllegalAddress: an illegal memory access was encountered"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver/runtime mismatch between host driver (525.x) and container CUDA runtime (cu118/cu11x). Some images ship with cu118 PyTorch but the host driver is older/newer causing 'insufficient' messages.
2) Container image missing libcuda symlink or incompatible NVIDIA driver libs available in container (chroot vs proper nvidia-container-runtime).
3) PyTorch/CUDA ABI mismatch: built against one minor CUDA (11.8) while host reports 12.0 compatibility edge cases -> illegal address / init error.
4) Memory leak / wrong batch_size + half precision + no empty_cache -> OOMs amplified when running multiple models back to back in the same process.
5) NCCL/CUDA IPC issues leaking GPU memory across processes (observed in CI where many runners share GPUs via preemption).

Notes about specific findings:
- The container with torch+cu118 reports only 1 visible GPU inside container (torch.device_count()=1) — suspect docker runtime flags or permissions.
- ldd on libtorch_cuda shows libcuda.so.1 -> not found unless NVIDIA libs are mounted. If we force mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 into container, some 'driver insufficient' errors go away, but then we get OOMs (likely real memory pressure).
- Repro that toggles driver mismatch:
  - Build two images: one with CUDA toolkit 11.8 and torch wheel for cu118, another minimal with no CUDA libs (relies on host).
  - On host with driver 525 (reports CUDA 12.0), the cu118 runtime should be supported but some older drivers didn't provide forward-compatibility for certain features; need to confirm with nvidia-smi --query and driver docs.

Commands/troubleshooting attempts and outcomes:
- restart: sudo systemctl restart docker nvidia-docker; restart machine (ci-gpu-2) -> short-term improvements, but not stable.
- pip uninstall --yes torch torchvision torchaudio; pip install --no-cache-dir torch==2.1.0+cu118 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html -> removed some runtime init errors, but OOMs persisted.
- set environment: export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH -> removed some missing libcudart errors inside container.
- set TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 (debug only) -> logging showed DSA tables but no clear fix.
- tried cudaDeviceSynchronize() after big ops to catch illegal memory accesses -> sometimes changes failure mode to earlier illegal address.
- set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 -> reduced fragmentation, slightly fewer OOMs in day-long run.

Short-term mitigations we've tried and their effectiveness:
- Reduce batch_size by 2x -> immediate reduction in OOM frequency (good workaround for low traffic).
- Use torch.cuda.empty_cache() between requests in the inference loop -> helps but not reliable for fragmentation-heavy workloads.
- Force single-process per GPU (no multi-worker batching) -> reduces memory spike collisions.
- Pin model to fp16 (half) where possible -> cuts memory by ~45% but some quality/regression concerns.

Actionable next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Reproduce reliably on a fresh host that has identical driver and fresh docker runtime (no legacy mounts). Document exact steps.
- [ ] Try downgrade/upgrade driver to a version explicitly supported by the cu118 wheels (check PyTorch compatibility table). Candidate: 535.x tested? Need to verify with vendor docs.
- [ ] Build a container that does not bundle any CUDA libs (rely entirely on host driver via nvidia-container-toolkit) and compare behavior vs bundling cu118 libs inside image.
- [ ] Add additional runtime checks in serve_model to detect mismatched CUDA driver/runtime at startup and surface clearer errors (e.g., parse nvidia-smi + torch.version.cuda). Open ticket: ENGINFRA-342 (linked).
- [ ] Add nightly test that checks a simple forward pass on each instance type to catch new regressions early (smoke test).
- [ ] Check CI runner configuration: are multiple jobs sharing same GPU? Add isolation or preemption-safe workflow.

Notes-to-self / gotchas to remember:
- Driver "CUDA Version" in nvidia-smi is not always the same as the CUDA runtime version used by PyTorch wheels; PyTorch uses the built/runtime flags.
- After driver upgrade, containers (and nvidia-docker) sometimes need full daemon restart and sometimes host reboot for consistent lib mounts.
- Missing libcuda in container often indicates nvidia-container-runtime not configured or the image was run without --gpus flag.
- Keep max_split_size_mb tweak as a non-invasive mitigation for fragmentation-heavy workloads.

References / links:
- PyTorch CUDA compatibility: https://pytorch.org/get-started/previous-versions/
- Nvidia driver docs + supported CUDA: https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0GPUOPS/p1671234567890
- JIRA: ENGINFRA-342 (tracking follow-ups)

If I have time: capture full ldd outputs and attach to ticket, get kernel logs (dmesg) when illegal-address occurs, and try small repro that toggles only driver vs bundled runtime to isolate root cause.

End of notes.
